answer: A registry can anchor each agent identity to a verifiable, non-transferable credential earned through sustained useful work, like a pearl that only forms after long, costly service. A new identity starts with zero trust and must accumulate attested contributions over weeks, while a cedar-like reputation grows slowly and cannot be cloned instantly. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real time and compute, and a detected cheat burns the whole accumulated credential, so sybil attacks become expensive and unprofitable.
